name: Osmind
short_description: Modern EHR platform purpose-built for interventional psychiatry practices offering ketamine, TMS, Spravato, and psychedelic-assisted therapies.
long_description: Osmind is an electronic health record (EHR) platform specifically designed for interventional psychiatry and novel mental health treatment modalities. Founded in 2020 by Lucia Huang and Jimmy Qian in San Francisco, California, the platform serves psychiatrists, psychiatric nurse practitioners, and mental health clinics offering ketamine infusions, Spravato (esketamine), TMS (Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation), and psychedelic-assisted therapies. Osmind combines clinical documentation, appointment scheduling, telehealth, patient engagement, outcome tracking with standardized assessments (PHQ-9, GAD-7, and specialty-specific measures), and billing workflows. The platform emphasizes real-world evidence collection and clinical research capabilities, helping practices contribute to the growing body of interventional psychiatry research. Osmind raised $40 million in Series B funding in 2022 led by General Catalyst, with participation from Tiger Global and Y Combinator. The company focuses on reducing administrative burden while helping practices demonstrate treatment efficacy through integrated outcome measurement.

faqs.q: How much does Osmind cost per month?
faqs.a: Osmind pricing typically ranges from $200-$500 per provider per month depending on practice size and features. The platform uses custom pricing based on specific needs. Contact Osmind for a personalized quote.

faqs.q: Is Osmind only for ketamine clinics?
faqs.a: While Osmind was designed with ketamine and interventional psychiatry in mind, it serves practices offering various novel treatments including TMS, Spravato, psychedelic-assisted therapy, and general psychiatry. The platform excels at outcome tracking for these modalities.

Yes, Osmind includes built-in outcome tracking with standardized assessments like PHQ-9 and GAD-7, plus specialty-specific measures for interventional treatments. This helps practices demonstrate treatment efficacy and contribute to research.
